h1:
Koh Samui Cooking Classes
Compared on Koh Samui
intro: Koh Samui has plenty of Thai cooking classes to choose from, and almost every one sells the same pitch: cook it yourself, eat what you made, and take the recipes home. But once you look closer, they differ quite a bit. Some are proper air-conditioned classrooms in the Chaweng area, some are small-group classes that walk you through a fresh market before you even step into the kitchen, and some are private classes that can fully adapt the menu for vegetarian or vegan diets. We compared 4 well-reviewed classes that are genuinely running on the island right now, and we'll tell you straight who each one suits best — whether it includes a market tour, how many dishes you get to make, what time slots run, and roughly what it costs — so you can pick the class that fits your style without having to guess.

blocks.html:
Cooking classes have become a favorite activity for visitors to Koh Samui, because you get more than just a meal of Thai food — you get to take the skill home with you. Most classes run for a half day, around 3 hours. Some start with a walk through a fresh market so you get to know the vegetables, curry pastes, and ingredients you can't easily find back home, then head into the kitchen to cook, dish by dish, finishing with a sit-down meal of what you made along with the recipes to take home.

What sets each class apart is in the details — whether it's an air-conditioned classroom or a relaxed home kitchen, whether a market tour is included or the focus is purely on the kitchen, whether it's a group class or a private class for just a couple of people, how freely you can choose your own menu, and how well it caters to vegetarian, vegan, or gluten-free diets. This article compares them clearly so you can see what each class is best at, so your money buys the exact experience you actually want.

blocks.caption: Comparing 4 Thai cooking classes on Koh Samui
rows: SITCA (Samui Institute of Thai Culinary Arts)

blocks.name: SITCA — Samui Institute of Thai Culinary Arts
blocks.bestFor: Anyone who wants a serious Thai cooking class in a proper air-conditioned classroom and to take recipes home — good for both beginners and cooking enthusiasts
blocks.duration: ~3 hrs per session (11:00 and 16:00 sessions, Monday-Saturday)
blocks.alt: Stir-frying Thai food in a wok with green chilies and fresh shrimp, similar to the atmosphere in a cooking class (illustrative image)

gallery.alt: Green curry served with rice, one of the Thai dishes you get to make hands-on in class (illustrative image)
A stall of fresh vegetables at a Thai market, the starting ingredients for the dishes you'll learn to cook (illustrative image)

blocks.descHtml:
SITCA, or the Samui Institute of Thai Culinary Arts, is a long-running Thai cooking school and the name that comes up most often when people staying on Koh Samui talk about looking for a cooking class. It's located in the Chaweng-Bophut area, an easy trip from accommodation in the central part of the island. Classes run in fixed sessions of about 3 hours each, with both an 11am and a 4pm slot, open Monday through Saturday. What sets it apart from typical home-style classes is that it's a genuine air-conditioned classroom with an individual station for each student — you cook every dish yourself, while the instructor demonstrates each step and explains the ingredients, curry pastes, and how to balance flavors the authentic Thai way. Some ingredients are prepped in advance for you, so you can focus on the actual technique. The menu rotates by day and session, and the class wraps up with everyone sitting down to eat what they made, plus a recipe booklet to take home.

Real reviews on Tripadvisor give this an average score of around 4.9 out of 5 from more than 350 reviewers. The common thread across reviews is that the instructors teach in detail and are approachable, explaining where each ingredient comes from and the reasoning behind the cooking technique — not just having you follow a recipe by rote. Many say the food came out tastier than expected and was the best Thai meal they'd ever cooked themselves. The kitchen is clean, the staff are attentive, and the class can accommodate vegetarian, vegan, and food-allergy needs. The price per person sits in the low four figures in baht, which many reviews consider good value for what you learn and eat.

One thing to know going in is that SITCA is primarily classroom-based — it doesn't include a walk through a fresh market like some other classes on the island. If a market tour is what you're after, look at one of the other options instead. Another point is that the menu for each session is a fixed set determined by the day, not something you can freely choose dish by dish. If there's a specific dish you really want to make, check that day's schedule before booking. During high season, sessions can get fairly full, so booking ahead and choosing a weekday will get you a more attentive experience.
blocks.tipHtml: Tip: Choose SITCA if you want a proper classroom-style class and don't mind skipping the market walk. Book ahead and pick a weekday session to avoid a crowded class. Check that day's menu schedule before booking, since each session runs a fixed set menu — and if you're vegetarian, vegan, or have food allergies, mention it when you book.
pros: Air-conditioned classroom with your own station, hands-on for every dish
Instructors teach in detail, explaining ingredient origins and flavor balance — a point many reviews agree on
Tripadvisor rating around 4.9 from 350+ reviews, accommodates vegetarian, vegan, and allergy needs
Ends with eating what you cooked plus a recipe booklet to take home
cons: No market tour — the focus is mainly classroom-based
Each session runs a fixed set menu by day, not a free choice of every dish
Sessions can get crowded during high season — book ahead and avoid holidays

blocks.name: Smiley Cook
blocks.bestFor: Anyone who wants a friendly small-group class with a fresh market tour and the freedom to choose their own dishes
blocks.duration: Half day (morning/afternoon session) · ~2 hrs cooking + 30-min market tour
blocks.alt: A fresh Thai market, the kind of place this class walks you through to pick ingredients before cooking (illustrative image)

gallery.alt: Pad Thai with shrimp, one of the dishes you can choose to make yourself in class (illustrative image)
Tom yum goong, a popular dish that students often choose to make in class (illustrative image)

blocks.descHtml:
Smiley Cook is a Thai cooking class in the Bophut-Chaweng area that's very well reviewed on Tripadvisor. Its clearest selling point is that it's a small-group class, limited to around 5 students per session, so instructors can give everyone proper attention and the atmosphere feels as relaxed as cooking with friends. The program starts with a roughly 30-minute fresh market tour, walking through herbs, vegetables, and spices used in Thai cooking, with a guide explaining the ingredients before heading back to the kitchen. Then comes about 2 hours of hands-on cooking, where you choose 4 dishes yourself from a popular list that includes pad Thai, som tam, green curry, and stir-fried beef with ginger. Free hotel pickup and drop-off is included.

Real reviews on Tripadvisor give this an average score of around 4.8 out of 5 from several hundred reviewers. A common theme is that the chef team is friendly and makes the class fun, and the market walk is a highlight that helps you understand Thai ingredients better. Many say they got to eat each dish as soon as it was cooked, rather than waiting until the whole class finished. Because the group is small, you get to ask questions and get real hands-on time — a good fit for couples and small groups of friends who want a warm experience rather than a large class.

Something to know is that because it takes so few people per session and is so well reviewed, spots fill up quickly — book ahead, especially during high season. And because it's a relaxed small-group class, anyone wanting a serious institute-style air-conditioned classroom might find it a bit too casual. Check the meeting point and pickup time clearly before class day, since the midday market walk can be fairly hot.
blocks.tipHtml: Tip: Book ahead since this class takes few people per session and fills up fast. Decide on the dishes you actually want to cook from the list before class day, and if you're vegetarian or have food allergies, mention it when booking — a small group makes it much easier to adjust the menu than a large class.
pros: Small group of around 5 max, instructors give everyone attention, friendly atmosphere
Includes a 30-minute fresh market tour and lets you choose 4 dishes to cook yourself
Tripadvisor rating around 4.8 from several hundred reviews, eat each dish as soon as it's done
cons: Takes few people per session and is well reviewed, so it fills up fast — book ahead
The relaxed vibe may not suit those wanting a serious institute-style classroom
The midday market walk can be hot — confirm your pickup time clearly

blocks.name: InFusion Cooking Classes Koh Samui
blocks.bestFor: Anyone who wants a private class for 1-2 people with a sea view, a free choice of menu, and full support for vegetarian, vegan, or gluten-free diets
blocks.duration: Half day, 3+ hrs (09:00-14:00 sessions · closed Sundays)

blocks.descHtml:
InFusion Cooking Classes is located in the Bophut area and is a very well-reviewed class on Tripadvisor that positions itself as a fairly premium option. What sets it apart from other classes on the island is that it's focused on being a private class, taking a maximum of around 1-2 people per session, so you get truly one-on-one attention from the instructor. The kitchen sits in a sea-view location overlooking the surrounding islands. The program starts with a market tour to pick out fresh ingredients, then heads back to the kitchen, where you can freely choose your dishes from a list of over 200 options, covering both savory dishes and desserts, with clear vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free choices. Classes are taught in multiple languages including English, French, and German. The price includes a recipe e-book to take home and cook from later.

Real reviews on Tripadvisor have been consistently positive, from nearly 300 reviewers. A common theme is the privacy and close attention you get — instructors explain in detail how each Thai ingredient works together with the others. Many reviewers who eat vegetarian or vegan say the menu was fully adapted for them without any drop in flavor. And because you choose your own dishes from such a long list, you actually get to cook what you want — a good fit for couples or anyone wanting a more personal experience than a group class.

One thing to accept is that the price is noticeably higher than typical classes on the island, since it's a private class and includes the recipe e-book. That price is worth it for anyone who values privacy and a free choice of menu, but if you want a more affordable group class, look elsewhere. It also only runs morning-to-afternoon sessions and is closed on Sundays, and because it's a private class, spots per session are very limited — book well ahead.
blocks.tipHtml: Tip: Choose InFusion if you value privacy and want to freely choose your own menu, especially if you're vegetarian, vegan, or gluten-free — mention it when booking, since this class can fully accommodate it. Because it's a private class with very limited spots, book well ahead and confirm your session doesn't fall on the Sunday closure.
pros: Private class for 1-2 people, one-on-one attention, sea-view kitchen
Free choice from a list of over 200 dishes, with clear vegetarian/vegan/gluten-free options
Consistently positive Tripadvisor reviews from nearly 300 reviewers, taught in multiple languages
Includes a market tour to pick ingredients and a recipe e-book to take home
cons: Noticeably more expensive than typical classes on the island
Very limited spots per session since it's a private class — book well ahead
Closed on Sundays — check the schedule before planning

blocks.name: Cook with Kookai
blocks.bestFor: Anyone who wants a warm home-kitchen class with an experienced chef, a morning market tour, and their own choice of dishes
blocks.alt: A fresh Thai market in the morning, where this class picks fresh ingredients before cooking (illustrative image)

gallery.alt: Tom yum goong, a popular dish you can choose to cook yourself in class (illustrative image)
A Thai stone mortar and pestle for pounding curry paste, equipment actually used in class (illustrative image)

blocks.descHtml:
Cook with Kookai is a home-kitchen-style Thai cooking class in the Maenam area on the northern side of Koh Samui. The chef and owner, Kookai, has more than 20 years of restaurant cooking experience. What sets this apart from institute-style classes is the warmth of genuinely learning in a Thai home. The program starts with a walk through the Maenam morning market to see fresh ingredients that just arrived that morning, with a stop for Thai coffee, before heading back to the chef's kitchen. You choose 4 dishes yourself from everyone's favorites, ranging from pad Thai to panang curry to mango sticky rice. The class runs about 3 hours or more and wraps up with everyone sitting down to eat what they made together.

Real reviews on Tripadvisor are consistently positive, even though the review count is still lower than the bigger names on the island. A common theme is that the chef is kind, patient, and makes the class fun, creating a warm, relaxed atmosphere like cooking at a relative's house. Many people who had never cooked Thai food before say they were able to go home and actually cook it themselves, and reviews also note that the menu can be adapted for vegetarian or vegan diets without issue. A good fit for anyone who wants a small, warm experience rather than a large or institute-style class.

Something to know is that the location is in the Maenam area on the north side of the island, so anyone staying in the Chaweng-Lamai zone should allow extra time and travel cost to get there and back. Check ahead whether that session includes pickup or if it costs extra. It's also a small class that doesn't take many people per session, and since the market tour happens in the morning, you'll need to head out early. Book ahead and confirm the meeting time clearly, and since the review count is still lower than the bigger operators, read the session details closely before booking to make sure it matches what you want.
blocks.tipHtml: Tip: Choose Cook with Kookai if you want a genuinely warm home-kitchen atmosphere and a real morning market tour. Check before booking whether your accommodation is in a zone with pickup included or whether it costs extra, since the location is in the Maenam area — and if you're vegetarian or vegan, just mention it when booking, since reviews confirm the menu can be adapted.
pros: Warm home kitchen with a chef who has 20+ years of restaurant experience
Includes a morning riverside market tour to pick fresh ingredients, plus your choice of 4 dishes
Real Tripadvisor reviews praise the chef as kind, patient, and fun to learn from
Menu can be adapted for vegetarian or vegan diets, as noted in reviews
cons: Located in the Maenam area to the north — guests staying in Chaweng-Lamai should allow extra time and transport cost
Review count is still lower than the bigger operators on the island — read the session details before booking
The market tour happens in the morning, so you'll need to head out early and confirm the meeting time in advance

blocks.title: How to pick a Koh Samui cooking class that's actually right for you
blocks.html:
First, choose between a classroom and a home kitchen. If you want a serious institute-style atmosphere in an air-conditioned room, SITCA suits that best. But if you prefer a warm, relaxed feeling like cooking at home, a small-group class like Smiley Cook or a home kitchen like Cook with Kookai will feel more like that.

Second, check whether a market tour is included. Many reviews say the market walk is the highlight, letting you get to know vegetables, curry pastes, and fresh ingredients you can't find at home. Smiley Cook, InFusion, and Cook with Kookai all include a market tour, while SITCA focuses on classroom teaching without a market walk. If that's what you want, skip the classroom-only option.

Third, consider group size and budget. If you want complete privacy and a free choice of menu, InFusion is a private class for 1-2 people but costs more. A small-group class like Smiley Cook is better value while still giving you plenty of attention. And finally, mention any dietary needs when you book. If you're vegetarian, vegan, or gluten-free, choose a class that clearly states it can accommodate you, like InFusion, or let a small-group class know in advance, since they tend to adapt menus easily.

faq.q: Which Koh Samui cooking classes include a market tour?
faq.a: Smiley Cook, InFusion, and Cook with Kookai all include a fresh market tour before heading into the kitchen. SITCA focuses on teaching in an air-conditioned classroom and does not include a market walk. If you want the market experience, which many reviews say is a highlight, choose one of the first three and confirm the session includes it before booking.

faq.q: How much do Koh Samui cooking classes cost?
faq.a: General group classes run around ฿1,500-2,200 per person for a half-day class that includes ingredients and a self-cooked meal. SITCA runs around ฿1,650-1,850, while InFusion, a private class for 1-2 people, starts around ฿4,990. Compare whether the price includes a market tour and hotel pickup, not just the number itself.

faq.q: Are there Koh Samui cooking classes that cater to vegetarian or vegan diets?
faq.a: Yes. InFusion clearly lists vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free options within its 200+ dish menu. Cook with Kookai has reviews confirming the recipe can be adapted for vegan or vegetarian diets, and both SITCA and Smiley Cook can adjust to a vegetarian menu if you let them know in advance. It's best to mention any dietary needs at the time of booking.

faq.q: How long do Koh Samui cooking classes take, and are they good for beginners?
faq.a: Most are half-day classes of around 3 hours (Smiley Cook, InFusion, and Cook with Kookai run about 3+ hours, while SITCA offers an 11am and a 4pm session). They're suitable for beginners, since instructors demonstrate and guide you step by step — many reviews from people who'd never cooked Thai food before say they were able to cook it again at home afterward. If you want closer attention, choose a small-group or private class.

faq.q: Should you book a Koh Samui cooking class in advance?
faq.a: Yes, you should book ahead, especially for small-group and private classes like Smiley Cook and InFusion, which take few people per session and fill up quickly during high season. Booking early also lets you flag any dietary needs and confirm hotel pickup in time before class day.
